html:
Yugoslavia, "land of the South Slavs", was a state in the western Balkans from 1918 to 1992. It joined Serbia and Montenegro with Slovenes, Croats and others who had lived under Austria-Hungary, plus lands taken from the Ottoman Empire in 1912 and 1913.

It began as the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes and took the name Yugoslavia in 1929. Serbs and Croats quarrelled over how centralised it should be. In 1941 the Axis invaded and split it up; a brutal war followed between occupiers, the Croatian fascist state, royalist Chetniks and the communist Partisans.

The Partisans won, and their leader Josip Broz Tito built a federal republic of six republics. He broke with Stalin in 1948 and helped found the Non-Aligned Movement. After Tito died in 1980 the federation weakened. From 1991 Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Macedonia broke away amid the Yugoslav Wars, the bloodiest in Europe since 1945.
